report.source_text: Subsequent CT angiogram confirmed a pulmonary sling, with the left pulmonary artery arising from the distal right pulmonary artery and wrapping around the distal trachea (Fig. 2). Left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction, consistent with left-sided air trapping, was observed. Moderate-sized patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and a notable patent foramen ovale (PFO) were present. Furthermore, a right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus) was identified (Fig. 3).

report.source_text: At 7-months-old the patient underwent left pulmonary artery sling and PDA repair with re-implantation of the left pulmonary artery into the main pulmonary artery anterior to the trachea and PDA division/ligation. She developed postoperative left pulmonary artery stenosis and underwent successful balloon angioplasty. Unfortunately, due to the significant left pulmonary artery hypoplasia she developed recurrent left pulmonary artery stenosis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: left pulmonary arterial sling with an associated right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-week-old female presented with respiratory distress and weight loss. Physical examination revealed a new cardiac murmur not previously documented. Initial echocardiography identified a left pulmonary arterial sling, prominent patent foramen ovale (PFO), and a moderate-sized patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) with continuous left-to-right shunting. Subsequent CT angiography confirmed the anatomic diagnosis: the left pulmonary artery arose from the distal right pulmonary artery and wrapped around the distal trachea, causing left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction with left-sided air trapping. Critically, CT imaging also identified a right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus). At 7 months of age, the patient underwent surgical repair consisting of left pulmonary artery re-implantation into the main pulmonary artery anterior to the trachea and PDA division/ligation. Post-operatively, she developed left pulmonary artery stenosis, which was treated with balloon angioplasty; however, recurrent stenosis developed secondary to significant left pulmonary artery hypoplasia.
